newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa Q1 shows strong savings, weak non-life.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa Q1 shows strong savings, weak non-life.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa confirmed current sector trends by presenting lower figures for non-life insurance and higher life and savings business when it released first quarter earnings on Tuesday.

Non-life insurance profit slipped to 94 million crowns ($11.9 million) from 98 million in the year earlier quarter, while life and savings operations swung to a profit of 96 million crowns from a loss of five million.
"The efforts we started in the savings market last year are now becoming apparent both in terms of sales volume and results," chief executive Lars Thunell said in an earnings statement.
"The greatest increase was in unit-linked insurance, which grew by more than 80 percent compared with the same period last year."

The total result jumped 45 percent to 950 million crowns, mainly following very favourable asset management and a continued stable trend in insurance operations. Earnings per share leaped to 14.10 crowns from 8.40 crowns.
Asset management showed investment income rising to 1.41 billion crowns from 992 million, of which 902 million consisted of realised gains, compared to 289 million in the year earlier quarter.
Those figures were boosted by an October 1996 decision to increase the share of equities in the investment portfolio.
"As a result of the favourable trend in the stock market, this (allocation) has contributed to the strong investment return despite a decline in the value of the bond portfolio," Trygg-Hansa said.
The market value of the equity portfolio amounted to 7.2 billion crowns on October 31, 1996, and 8.5 billlion on March 31 this year, corresponding to 41 percent of the group's investment assets.
Pre-tax profit surged to 1.18 billion crowns from 741 million, largely supported by 'other operations' generating a profit of 1.11 billion crowns, up from 644 million crowns.
But life insurance plunged further into the red on a pre-tax basis by showing a loss of 22 million crowns compared to a one million crown loss in the first quarter of 1996.
Total gross premiums written slipped to 3.35 billion crowns from 3.38 billion with figures for non-life insurance falling to 1.67 billion crowns from 2.01 billion.
"The decrease in (non-life) premiums is mainly attributable to lower volumes and rate reductions in industrial and commercial insurance," the company said.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017 ($ = 7.884 Swedish Crowns)
